sections.h2: What does the Paulding County recorder do?
sections.html:
The Paulding County Recorder keeps the permanent record of real estate documents for every parcel in the county, including deeds, mortgages and easements. The office is in the courthouse at 115 N. Williams Street in the village of Paulding, which is also the county seat.

The recorder's website says its records search is open around the clock at no direct cost to the user. The office does not write deeds, so a seller whose paperwork needs drafting should use an attorney or the title company handling the sale.

Paulding County runs on a small footprint. The Census Bureau counts 18,727 residents in July 2025 across about 416 square miles of land, which works out to roughly 45 people per square mile.

sections.h2: How do you record a deed in Paulding County?
sections.html:
Most sellers never carry the deed anywhere, because the closing agent records it. If you handle it yourself, the deed first goes to the county auditor for transfer, then to the recorder.

The county accepts electronic recording through three vendors listed on the recorder's site: CSC, ePN and Simplifile. The page says documents can be submitted for eRecording Monday through Friday from 8:00 am until 3:00 pm.

Before the deed is signed, check these points:

  • The seller signs before a notary or another officer listed in Revised Code 5301.01, and the acknowledgment is certified on the deed.
  • The deed gives the grantee's tax mailing address and refers to the previous recorded instrument, because the auditor needs both under section 319.20.
  • The page layout meets the state margin and print rules, or an extra charge applies.

sections.h2: What are the recording fees in Paulding County?
sections.html:
The state sets the base schedule: the Ohio Recorders Association lists $34.00 for the first two pages of a deed or mortgage and $8.00 for each page after that. A county may add a preservation surcharge of up to $5.00 per document, and that amount varies by county. Call the Paulding County Recorder for the final figure before you send a check.

Common Ohio recording charges (Ohio Recorders Association fee page and Revised Code 317.32)
ItemCharge
Deed or mortgage, first two pages$34.00
Each added page$8.00
Document that does not meet the state layout rules$20.00 extra
Document needing a marginal reference, such as a release$4.00 per reference added
Preservation surchargeUp to $5.00, set by the county

The $20 layout charge applies to documents prepared after June 30, 2009 that miss the rules: 10 point type or larger, black or blue ink, a 3 inch top margin on page one, and 1 inch margins on the sides and bottom.

sections.h2: What should a Paulding County seller check before signing the deed?
sections.html:
A short checklist prevents most rejections at the auditor's or recorder's counter.

  • Confirm the seller's name on the deed matches the name on the last recorded deed. Differences need an explanation or an affidavit.
  • Gather the payoff statement for any mortgage and expect a recorded release to follow after closing.
  • Have the buyer's full tax mailing address ready, since the auditor enters it on the tax list.
  • If part of a tract is being sold, ask the auditor and the county engineer whether the new description needs approval. Ohio law lets each county adopt its own conveyance standards.
  • Bring a check for the exact conveyance fee, because Paulding's auditor says other amounts will not be processed.

The title company or closing attorney usually handles all of this on a sale. On a cash sale to a buyer who closes quickly, the same items still apply, so find them before you set a closing date.

sections.h2: What does the Paulding County auditor charge on a sale?
sections.html:
The auditor collects a conveyance fee and a transfer fee before the deed goes to the recorder. The Paulding County Auditor's website states the conveyance fee as $4.00 per thousand of the purchase price and the transfer fee as $.50 per parcel.

The auditor adds a practical rule: checks must be for the exact amount of the conveyance fee or the conveyance will not be processed. Paulding's site has a conveyance calculator under its Tools menu, so use it for your own price instead of estimating.

The seller pays these charges under section 319.202(D). Form DTE 100 goes with a regular sale, and form DTE 100 (EX) is used to claim an exemption from the conveyance fee. If the deed also conveys mineral rights or a manufactured home, ask the auditor how it is handled.

sections.h2: What does the Census say about Paulding County homes?
sections.html:
Paulding County is a small, owner-heavy market. The 2020 to 2024 American Community Survey figures posted by the Census Bureau show the following for the county.

  • Owner-occupied housing unit rate: 80.1%.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $140,800.
  • Median gross rent: $812 a month.
  • Households: 7,624, averaging 2.45 persons.
  • Housing units on July 1, 2025: 8,597.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 28.

Twenty-eight permits across eleven villages and the farm townships is a low count, and the Census Bureau reports that 90.6% of residents lived in the same house a year earlier.

sections.h2: What does the Paulding County economy look like for a house seller?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counts 309 employer establishments in the county in 2023, with total employment of 4,033, down 2.6% from 2022. The 2020 to 2024 survey puts 62.6% of residents age 16 and over in the civilian labor force, and the mean travel time to work is 24.0 minutes.

Census figures for 2022 business receipts show where the business base sits: about $56.0 million in transportation and warehousing, $50.4 million in health care and social assistance, and $137.3 million in retail sales. Median household income for 2020 to 2024 is $67,731, and 10.4% of residents are in poverty.

The median home value of $140,800 sits well under the $191,100 posted for Perry County and the $256,800 for Pickaway County in the same Census comparison.

sections.h2: Where are the places a Paulding County seller might own property?
sections.html:
The county has eleven villages: Antwerp, Broughton, Cecil, Grover Hill, Haviland, Latty, Melrose, Oakwood, Paulding, Payne and Scott. Public school districts serving the county include Antwerp Local, Paulding Exempted Village and Wayne Trace Local, and Vantage Career Center serves students from the area.

The land is very flat. Wikipedia describes Paulding County as lying entirely within the old Great Black Swamp, with roads laid out about every mile, and the county is crossed by U.S. Routes 127, 24 and 30 and by the Auglaize and Maumee rivers.

Where a farm parcel is being split, the new description has to be reviewed before the auditor will transfer it. Ask the auditor and the county engineer what they need.

sections.h2: How do you find a recorded deed or a mortgage release in Paulding County?
sections.html:
Use the records search on the recorder's website, which links to an Ava web portal. The recorder's site also has a property fraud alert page and a notary fraud alert sign-up, which notify an owner when a document is recorded under a name they enter.

A paid-off mortgage shows up as a recorded release. If a seller is not sure a prior loan was released, look for it before listing, because an open mortgage in the records will come up at closing.

For a quick sale, an investor buyer or a title company will order this search anyway. Having the old deed and any release ready shortens the wait.

faqs.q: Where is the Paulding County Recorder's office?
faqs.a: The recorder's office is in the Paulding County courthouse at 115 N. Williams Street in Paulding, Ohio. The recorder's website also links to maps and to records search pages.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed electronically in Paulding County?
faqs.a: Yes. The recorder accepts eRecording through CSC, ePN and Simplifile, Monday through Friday from 8:00 am until 3:00 pm.

faqs.q: How much is the conveyance fee in Paulding County?
faqs.a: The county auditor states it as $4.00 per thousand of the purchase price, plus a $.50 per parcel transfer fee. Use the auditor's online conveyance calculator for your price.
No. The office records documents but does not draft them. Have an attorney or a title company prepare the deed.

faqs.q: What is the extra $20 charge on a deed?
faqs.a: It is the state non-standard document fee under Revised Code 317.114. It applies when a document does not follow the margin, ink and type size rules, so check the layout before signing.
